chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Financing the band himself and its collapse
summary: Without MCA's bookings Wilson ran out of money, buying uniforms and arrangements himself; Ben left, Tab Smith and Bob Carroll followed and the draft hit the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And that big band of mine, finally, without the cooperation of the booking office, I couldn't pay the man and I had already invested all of my savings from working with Benny Goodman.

I had to finance the band myself, you know, get them the uniforms and the PA set to carry around on the road with us, and buying arrangements and the stands, and all the equipment you need to run a big band, I had done that myself rather than borrow money to pay it back. I could have borrowed money at exorbitant interest, like at 40% interest, but I had saved up money from Goodman to do it myself.

But the money began to run out, and without the cooperation of MCA, the booking office, to book us in decent jobs and keep it going, the band began falling apart, and this way, the person -- when Ben left, Duke got Ben, and I got a good man in Ben's place, in Tab Smith. Now Tab was a great alto player who switched to tenor.
Oh yes, I know Tab. He was with Chick
Tab? I'm not sure. But Tab was on alto, but he came to my big band, and he did a good job sitting in Ben's chair playing all the solos that Ben had played and meeting the part.
And something happened -- Tab left and then I finally got a good man with a big sound named Bob Carroll.
Oh yeah, I know Bob Carroll.
Right. But then Bob got drafted in the army, and the Second World War was coming, you know, and this was about 1940 and they were put on the draft, and everybody went --
